name: simsched
algorithm: a seeded deterministic scheduler with a simulated clock: n tasks each sleep 1 ms of simulated time and send their index to one channel, r times, and a collector receives all n * r values; Mk under one std.sim Sim, Go in one testing/synctest bubble (README.md).

skip.c: no std scheduler with a simulated clock
skip.rust: no std scheduler with a simulated clock
skip.zig: no std scheduler with a simulated clock

notes: Written by std-sim for SIM-R21 and SIM-R20 (status/std-sim.md). Go's testing/synctest (GA in Go 1.25) runs goroutines in a bubble whose fake clock jumps when every goroutine is durably blocked: the same job as std.sim's discrete-event clock. synctest.Test needs a *testing.T, so the Go program runs one test through testing.Main with the testing package's own output sent to the null device.

Go's bubble runs goroutines in parallel between clock jumps; std.sim runs one task at a time in a seeded order, which is the point of it, so the Mk column also pays a park and a grant per sleep and per blocking channel operation.
